searchText: Following on my takeaway from the last implementers call, I've reworked my websockets implementation of discv5 transport somewhat and built out the simple proxy/UDP relay that <@!364458974906548225> mentioned so now browser based discv5 clients can interact with the UDP based clients via the relay and it's transparent to the broader network It's only a proof of concept at this point but it allows browser based nodes to complete the discv5 handshake and exchange packets successfully as long as the proxy stays up. Very cool to have this concept validated. If anyone wants to take a look - this very simple react app https://github.com/acolytec3/discv5-browser and this proxy https://github.com/acolytec3/ultralight-proxy make it work start the proxy and then the react app. The discv5 client is available in the browser console with `discv5.addEnr(...` or `discv5.findNode(...` yep, this makes sense, thanks I'll be skipping today's call as I got sick. I didn't get to creating the issue to discuss on the reuse of the different network protocols / overlay abstractions, but I'll try to get to that soon. Implementers call in 5 minutes: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82763999854?pwd=Uy9sR1ZxeUJhc0crckFKanV5VERCdz09
